title: What are the mean and median heights of your class?
description: The book asks for the mean and median of the heights of your own class. Ten sample heights are sorted, then the mean, the median and the gap from shortest to tallest are found and shown on a dot plot.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same four steps describe the heights of any class: sort, find the mean, find the median, draw the dot plot. Watch for children who forget to sort before taking the middle value.

video_script.why: The child can find the mean and median and now collects real data.
video_script.substitution: Measure, sort, compute and plot: the same four steps for any class.
video_script.anchor: Sample heights in cm of ten students, labelled sample: 138, 142, 145, 147, 150, 151, 151, 153, 156, 160
video_script.payoff_line: Use the same steps for your own class.

final_answer.value: For the sample data: mean 149.3 cm, median 150.5 cm, range 22 cm; use the same steps for your own class
final_answer.spoken: use the same steps for your own class

hold_back: same steps for your own class
maths_rules: gap 160 - 138 = 22 cm; dot plot from 135 to 160; most dots from 145 to 156
with your own class: measure, sort, then find the mean and median and draw the dot plot
video_script.design: One row of ten sample heights, sorted. The mean and median are marked on the same number line as the dot plot.
open_questions: The book asks about the viewer's own class, so the ten heights are sample data supplied by the worklist and are labelled sample on screen.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Sort the heights from least to greatest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The total divided by the number of values is called the mean.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The middle of the sorted list is called the median.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>A dot plot puts one dot on a number line for each height.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

marks.m1: the word sample and the list are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, ten sample heights in centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They are one hundred and thirty eight, one hundred and forty two and one hundred and forty five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then come one hundred and forty seven, one hundred and fifty and one hundred and fifty one.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Then come one hundred and fifty one, and one hundred and fifty three.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The last two are one hundred and fifty six and one hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: mean, median and a dot plot of the heights

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the mean and the median, and show the heights on a dot plot.

marks.m1: the list is checked from least to greatest

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, put the ten heights in order from least to greatest. These samples are already in order.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The shortest is one hundred and thirty eight and the tallest is one hundred and sixty.

marks.m2: the ten heights are added and 1493 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, find the mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The ten heights add up to one thousand four hundred and ninety three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Divide by ten. The mean is one hundred and forty nine point three centimetres.

beats.on_screen: 10 values, so the median is halfway between the 5th and 6th: (150 + 151) ÷ 2 = 301 ÷ 2 = 150.5 cm

marks.m1: the fifth and sixth values glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, find the median. Ten is even, so it lies halfway between the fifth and sixth values.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Those are one hundred and fifty and one hundred and fifty one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Add them to get three hundred and one. Half of that is one hundred and fifty point five centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, find the gap between the tallest and the shortest. One hundred and sixty take away one hundred and thirty eight is twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Draw one dot for each height on a line. The line runs from one hundred and thirty five to one hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Most dots lie from one hundred and forty five to one hundred and fifty six.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check the answers. The mean must lie between the shortest and the tallest, and it does.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five heights lie below the median and five above.
